provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Love your neighbour
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state ways to show love to friends.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate kindness to classmates.
Introduction:
We love our families. Today we learn to love our friends too.
Content:
Love your neighbour means to be kind to everyone around you. We share our toys with friends. We help friends when they fall. We use kind words like please and thank you. When we see a friend sad, we comfort them. We do not take things that belong to others.
Class activity:
Let us play a game. I will say a situation. You show how to be kind with your face and hands.
Evaluation questions:
What does love your neighbour mean?
How do you show love to a friend?
What should you do if you see a friend crying?
Summary:
We must be kind and loving to all our friends and classmates.

topics.title: Respect for God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to show respect to God.
The pupils should be able to explain why we behave well in holy places.
Introduction:
God created us and gives us food. We must show respect to God.
Content:
We show respect to God by praying before we eat. We pray when we wake up and before sleeping. We behave well in church or mosque. We do not shout in holy places. We listen to our teachers about God. We thank God for our good things.
Class activity:
Let us practice folding our hands and closing our eyes to pray quietly.
Evaluation questions:
When should we pray?
How do we behave in church or mosque?
Why do we thank God?
Summary:
We show respect to God through prayer and good behavior.

topics.title: Hard work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we finish our tasks.
The pupils should be able to identify work before play.
Introduction:
We have small jobs to do in class. Let us learn about working hard.
Content:
Hard work means doing our tasks well. We finish our little tasks like arranging chairs. We put our toys back in the box. We clean our tables after eating. Work before play means we do our jobs before we play. When we work first, we feel happy after playing.
Class activity:
Let us clean our classroom together. Each child will wipe one table.
Evaluation questions:
What does hard work mean?
What should we do before we play?
How do you feel after finishing your work?
Summary:
We must work hard and finish our tasks before playing.

topics.title: Contentment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what contentment means.
The pupils should be able to explain why we should not cry for everything.
Introduction:
Sometimes we want many things. Today we learn to be happy with what we have.
Content:
Contentment means being happy with what you have. We should not cry for everything we see. If a friend has a new toy, we can be happy for them. We can enjoy our own toys too. We say thank you for what we have. We do not fight to have what others have.
Class activity:
Let us show our favorite toy and tell why we like it.
Evaluation questions:
What does contentment mean?
What should you do when a friend has a new toy?
Why is it good to be happy with what you have?
Summary:
We should be content and thank God for what we have.

topics.title: Honesty pays
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why honesty is important.
The pupils should be able to tell the story of an honest child.
Introduction:
Sometimes we want to hide mistakes. Today we learn about telling the truth.
Content:
Honesty means telling the truth always. The story of the honest child shows this. The child broke a cup but told the truth. Truth brings trust from parents and teachers. When we are honest, people believe us. Being honest makes us feel good inside.
Class activity:
Let us practice saying the truth. I will ask questions. Answer truthfully.
Evaluation questions:
What does honesty mean?
Why does truth bring trust?
How do you feel when you tell the truth?
Summary:
Honesty is good because it makes people trust us.

topics.title: Unity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we should be united.
The pupils should be able to list ways to play with every child.
Introduction:
We are all in the same class. We must love and play together.
Content:
Unity means working and playing together. We are one class, one Nigeria. We share toys with all children. We do not leave anyone out when playing. We help friends who cannot do things well. When we are united, we are strong and happy.
Class activity:
Let us hold hands and sing a song about unity.
Evaluation questions:
What does unity mean?
How can we play with every child?
Why is it good to be united?
Summary:
We must be united and play with everyone in our class.

topics.title: Service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what service means.
The pupils should be able to identify little jobs to help others.
Introduction:
We can help others without being told. This is called service.
Content:
Service means helping others without being asked. We help by cleaning the classroom. We help by picking up things that fell. We help friends who need help. We look around for little jobs to do. Service makes our class a happy place.
Class activity:
Let us find one job to help in our classroom and do it now.
Evaluation questions:
What does service mean?
Give one way to help in class.
How does service make people feel?
Summary:
We should serve others by helping without being asked.

topics.title: Forgiveness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what forgiveness means.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to make peace.
Introduction:
Sometimes friends hurt us. Today we learn to forgive and make peace.
Content:
Forgiveness means letting go of small hurts. We forgive when someone says sorry. We do not stay angry for a long time. We make peace before going home. We shake hands and say sorry to friends. Forgiveness helps us to be happy.
Class activity:
Let us practice saying sorry and shaking hands with a friend.
Evaluation questions:
What does forgiveness mean?
What should you do when someone says sorry?
Why is it good to forgive others?
Summary:
We must forgive others to have peace and happiness.

topics.title: Being a good example
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why younger children copy us.
The pupils should be able to list ways to behave well.
Introduction:
Little children watch us and copy what we do.
Content:
Younger children copy everything we do. They copy our words and actions. We must behave well always. We use kind words when talking. We share our things with others. We follow class rules. Being a good example helps others learn good behavior.
Class activity:
Let us show a good action that younger children can copy.
Evaluation questions:
Why do younger children copy us?
How can we be a good example?
What happens when we behave well?
Summary:
We must be good examples for younger children to copy.

topics.title: Revision and character day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite all moral rules learned.
The pupils should be able to identify the kindest friend in class.
Introduction:
Today we remember all we learned about good behavior.
Content:
We recite our moral rules about love, respect, hard work, contentment, honesty, unity, service, forgiveness and being a good example. We think about who has been the kindest friend. We award the kindest friend with a special clap. We celebrate good character in our class.
Class activity:
Let us stand up and say all our moral rules together.
Evaluation questions:
Name one moral rule we learned.
Who has shown kindness this week?
Why is it good to have good character?
Summary:
We remember our moral rules and celebrate good character.
